title: Live-cell fluorescence-guided cryoFIB-milling and electron cryo-tomography of virus-infected cells
author: Franken, Rosch, et al.
materials: Whole cells are only transparent to the electron beam in the cell periphery. If the area of interest is deeper inside the cell, cryoFIB-milling is a mandatory step. In this process, material of the cell is ablated by a focused ion beam in such a way that only a thin lamella through the cell is left. The thickness of such lamellae is typically ∼200 nm, being thin enough to be directly transmitted by the electron beam (Marko et al., 2006; Villa et al., 2013). The procedure described here is based on an Aquilos 2 cryo-FIB system (Thermo Fisher Scientific™), which has MAPS software installed and is equipped with the AutoTEM (Kuba et al., 2021) software for automated lamella milling. Alternatively, lamellae can be milled manually or with the help of academic auto-milling software (Klumpe et al., 2021; Zachs et al., 2020; Buckley et al., 2020).

steps.title: Split A549 cell culture
steps.instruction: Preheat PBS, trypsin, and growth medium to 37 °C; check confluence with a light microscope; remove medium; wash cells with 5 mL PBS; add 2 mL trypsin and incubate 10 min (or until cells detach); stop reaction with 3 mL growth medium; transfer 0.5–1 mL (for splitting after 3–4 days) or 2 mL (for next‑day use) of the cell suspension to a new 10 cm dish, add 10 mL growth medium; if >2 mL transferred, spin down 2 min at 300 rcf and discard supernatant; place dish in a 37 °C incubator with 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Preheat PBS, trypsin, and growth medium to 37 °C.
Check cell confluence under a light microscope.
Remove old medium from the culture dish.
Wash cells once with 5 mL PBS.
Add 2 mL trypsin, incubate 10 min (or until cells are loose).
Stop trypsinisation with 3 mL growth medium.
Add 0.5–1 mL (3–4 day split) or 2 mL (next‑day split) of suspension to a new 10 cm dish and add 10 mL growth medium.
If using >2 mL, centrifuge 2 min at 300 rcf and discard supernatant.
Incubate the new dish at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Clip grids into Autogrids
steps.instruction: Clip the electron‑microscopy grids into Autogrid carriers as described in step 40 to enable safe transfer to the cryo‑FIB system.

steps.title: Cool Aquilos loading station
steps.instruction: Fill the Aquilos 2 loading station with liquid nitrogen and wait until bubbling subsides to a minimal level.

steps.title: Transfer Autogrid assemblies to shuttle
steps.instruction: Pick 1–2 Autogrid assemblies from the storage box, orient them with cells facing up using the mark opposite the cut‑out, place them into the FIB/SEM shuttle, slowly flip the shuttle into loading position and verify that the assemblies are securely fixed.

steps.title: Insert shuttle into microscope chamber
steps.instruction: Using an evacuated transfer rod, move the shuttle from the loading station into the microscope chamber; complete the transfer within 4 min to avoid devitrification.

steps.title: Inspect grids with SEM and acquire images
steps.instruction: Acquire low‑magnification SEM overviews of both grids, adjust focus and working distance, and take tiled SEM maps; if fluorescence data are available, import the fluorescence image into MAPS, rescale if necessary, and align it to the SEM image using the 3‑point method.

substeps.instruction: Take low‑mag SEM overview of each grid.
Increase magnification to focus and set working distance.
Collect tiled SEM maps with MAPS.
Import fluorescence image (right‑click → Import Images).
Rescale image if too large.
Align fluorescence to SEM using 3‑point method (accurate, well‑spaced points).
Confirm alignment and finalize.

steps.title: Select lamella sites in MAPS
steps.instruction: Based on the combined fluorescence and SEM information, save lamella positions in MAPS, preferring single cells, avoiding broken squares, and staying at least four grid squares away from the edge of a 200‑mesh grid.

steps.title: Apply platinum sputter coat
steps.instruction: Deposit a platinum layer with the sputter coater at 1 kV, 30 mA for 10 s to reduce charging before further imaging.

steps.title: Open AutoTEM and load project
steps.instruction: Launch the AutoTEM software and import the MAPS project that contains the selected lamella sites.

steps.title: Configure milling template
steps.instruction: Select a milling template appropriate for the cell type (e.g., lamella width 12 µm, depth 2 µm); use the default depth correction of 100 % and set a 1 µm milling offset for each step; note that the template cannot be changed after the preparation step.

steps.title: Run preparation milling step
steps.instruction: Execute the preparation step in AutoTEM, allowing a target milling angle of approximately 8 °; if eucentricity fails, mill a nearby mark and use a maximal tilt step of 5 °.

steps.title: Deposit organic platinum with GIS
steps.instruction: Using the gas injection system, deposit an organic platinum layer for 17 s, creating an ~4 µm protective coating on each grid.

steps.title: Perform automated milling (no thinning)
steps.instruction: Start the automated milling sequence without the thinning stage; ensure the ice layer around cells is sufficient for stability; automated thinning can be enabled later only if sample conditions allow.

steps.title: Manual polishing of lamellae
steps.instruction: After auto‑milling (lamellae ≈ 500 nm), manually thin/polish each lamella at 30 pA; create polish patterns 1 µm narrower than the void; if the GIS coat hangs, polish only the top surface; aim for final thickness of 200–500 nm depending on experimental goals.

substeps.instruction: Select a lamella in AutoTEM site list and choose ‘polish’.
Set ion beam current to 30 pA.
Draw polish patterns 1 µm narrower than the void.
If GIS coat hangs, polish only the top surface.
Check lamella thickness (target 200–500 nm).

steps.title: Final sputter coating
steps.instruction: Apply a final sputter coat at 1 kV, 7 mA for 5 s to increase conductivity for TEM imaging and prevent charging.

steps.title: Record final overview and angles
steps.instruction: Acquire a final SEM overview of the milled grids and note the milling angle of each lamella for later tomogram setup.

steps.title: Unload and store grids
steps.instruction: Remove the sample from the FIB‑SEM using clean liquid nitrogen, transfer it to the loading station within 4 min, place the Autogrid boxes back into LN₂ storage; grids can be stored indefinitely, although ice contamination may accumulate over time.

substeps.instruction: Unload sample with clean LN₂ to avoid contamination.
Transfer to loading station quickly (≤ 4 min).
Store Autogrid boxes in LN₂.
Note that grids may be kept indefinitely, but monitor for ice buildup.

description: This protocol describes the case of studying human adenovirus late stages of infection in A549 cells, from infection and seeding on grids to cryoET. It has been applied to determine the nuclear egress pathway of adenovirus, which starts around 48 h after infection (Pfitzner et al., 2021). However, the same protocol can be applied to study different time-points of infections, different cell lines, cells infected with different pathogens, uninfected cells and cells expressing other fluorescent reporter-proteins. Along the descriptions, notes can be found that include small variations, and useful handling tips, provided in a detail that stands out from a scientific paper’s methods section. Our workflow (Figure 1) is adjusted to the infrastructure available at the Advanced Light and Fluorescence Microscopy (ALFM) facility at the Centre for Structural Systems Biology (CSSB) and the CryoEM Facility at the CSSB. While fluorescence microscopy is not heavily dependent on the type of microscope, the CryoEM Facility has the electron microscopes from Thermo Fisher Scientific, which have a grid-holder system based on Autogrids. While it is expected that our protocol can be adjusted to other systems, this has not been tested and might need some adjusting.Figure 1Overview of the described workflow, the corresponding steps in this protocol as well as their durations Depending on your country’s legislation, the experiments may need to be approved by authorities prior to starting, and standard operation procedures may need to be implemented including the handling of the pathogen and of the contaminated liquid nitrogen. HAdV5-pIX-mcherry is classified at biosafety level 2 (BSL2) in Germany. The described experiments were conducted in BLS 2 laboratories, and safety measures and experiments have been approved by the government of the Hanseatic City of Hamburg before they were conducted.
